subject: [hw] DEC02 -> K02/DEC01: larb SLP_CON release is 0x10000 (not 0) and the racing restore runs at LOCK_LAT with CORE off
body:
Two measured interface findings from the DEC02 trace (DEC01 client + T02 fake, 320x240 12 AUs and 1080p 6 AUs, host only).

1) LARB SLP_CON RELEASE WRITE IS 0x00010000, NOT 0.
The vendor handshake per core per AU, at 0x1600d00c (larb5, LAT) and 0x1602e00c (larb4, CORE), is:
  R 0x0d00c = 0x00000000
  R 0x0d00c = 0x00000000
  W 0x0d00c = 0x00000001     <- request sleep
  R 0x0d00c = 0x00010001     <- poll ack bit 16
  ... (later) W 0x0d00c = 0x00010000   <- release: whole word read back, bit 0 cleared, bit 16 still set
Exactly 1 request + 1 release per larb per AU: 18 of each value per larb over 12+6 AUs. No other offset of either page is written (checked: the write set is exactly {0x0d00c, 0x2e00c}).
K02's allow-list as described ("WRITE_MASK mask 1, or value & ~1 == 0") accepts the request and REFUSES the release (18 EACCES per session). It must also accept 0x00010000, or the client/client-visible return of the release write fails. Suggested rule for the two words: allow RWVC_OP_WRITE when (value & ~0x10001u) == 0, i.e. only bits 0 and 16, and keep every other offset of pages 0x0d/0x2e EACCES.
Evidence: gpu/hwcodec/facts/vdec_trace/PAGES.md section 4 (values and counts); raw trace /tmp/n2hw-dec02/t320b-1.trace lines 181-199, 637-655; classify.py now checks the value set.

2) THE RACING RESTORE HAPPENS AT LOCK_LAT, i.e. WITH CORE OFF (DEC01 item).
DEC01's client answers the daemon's LOCK_LAT by powering VDEC_SOC, restoring the 68 racing words at 0x16004100..0x1600420c and only then powering VDEC_CORE -- the order of mtk_vcodec_dec_clock_on() (mt6885/mtk_vcodec_dec_pm.c:184-213 restores in both branches; the MTK_VDEC_LAT branch enables only MT_CG_SOC and MT_CG_VDEC1). With the current kernel/fake map (VDEC_RACING -> RWVC_BLK_VDEC_CORE) that write is refused: 12 EACCES per 12-AU session, one per AU, at 0x16004100.
This is not a request to change K02's conservative map (CORE takes a hidden SOC reference, so it is safe for every vendor access -- those all happen with both domains on; the physical MTCMOS of the page is [I]). Two legal fixes:
  (a) hw-dec01: in dec_lock(), on the first active user take BOTH blocks (SOC and CORE) for the active period, then restore the racing words. Android has both domains on during a decode, so this matches the phone even if the page is SOC; or
  (b) hw-k02: allow the racing page (0x16004000, and by the same address split 0x16000000) while only SOC is on.
My harness stages (the fake-side equivalent of) (b) in /tmp so the trace is clean; PAGES.md states the measured fact and marks the physical domain [I].

Not blocking DEC02. Host only, no phone, nothing published.
